Minerva unveils Roger for hazardous work with $10 million in funding

Roger combines AI-assisted mobility with specialist control through VR, with paid pilots planned for the fall.

Minerva Humanoids / GlobeNewswire ↗6 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

Funding supports initial field pilots

Minerva Humanoids emerged on October 6 with approximately $10 million in pre-seed funding led by General Catalyst, with Long Journey Ventures and Credo Ventures as co-leads. Roger targets hazardous onshore and offshore energy work and public-safety applications. The company plans its first paid pilots for the fall.

Specialists retain critical control

Roger is semi-autonomous. Minerva Intelligence manages balance, fall recovery and navigation while translating remote operator input into movement. A specialist uses a VR headset to see through the robot and perform fine manipulation. The intended model preserves human judgment for critical actions rather than giving a robot independent authority over hazardous work.

A prototype is not broad deployment

Minerva says it developed a walking prototype in five months. Initial units are manufactured and assembled in Germany, with production planned in Germany and the US. Rapid development does not establish reliability in every field condition. Pilot results will need to demonstrate communication quality, controllability and resilience as operating environments change.
